{{Short description|British periodical (1841–1871)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2019}}
{{Italic title}}
'''''The Lady's and Gentleman's Diary''''' was a [[recreational mathematics]] magazine formed as a successor of ''[[The Ladies' Diary]]'' and ''[[Gentleman's Diary]]'' in 1841. It was published annually between 1841 and 1871<ref name=iona/> by the Company of Stationers; its editor from 1844 to 1865 was [[Wesley S. B. Woolhouse]]. It consisted mostly of problems posed by its readers, with their solutions given in later volumes, though it also contained word puzzles and poetry. The magazine was based in [[London]]. It ceased publication in 1871.<ref name="iona">{{cite book|author=Iona Italia|title=The Rise of Literary Journalism in the Eighteenth Century: Anxious Employment|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DxKtVeAoVSUC&pg=PA5|accessdate=22 October 2016|year=2005|publisher=Psychology Press|isbn=978-0-415-34392-3|page=5}}</ref> This should not be confused with ''Ladies and Gentlemens Diary, or Royal Almanack'' (1775 to 1786) which was printed by Thomas Carnan and edited by [[Reuben Burrow]] and was a short lived competitor to ''The Ladies' Diary''.

[[Kirkman's schoolgirl problem]] originated in a question in the magazine.
